verses.t: (To THE BRIDE) Repeat after me: "I, Mary, take thee, John, to be my aseptic and eugenic husband, to have and to hold from this day forward, for better, for worse, for richer, for poorer, to love, to cherish and to nurse, till death do us part; and thereto I give thee my troth."

(THE BRIDE duly promises. THE BEST MAN _then hands over the ring, which_ THE CLERGYMAN _drops into the bichloride. It turns green. He fishes it up again, wipes it dry with a piece of aseptic cotton and presents it to_ THE BRIDEGROOM, who places it upon the third finger of THE BRIDE'S left hand. Then THE CLERGYMAN goes on with the ceremony, THE BRIDEGROOM repeating after him.)
